title: Two sides, one centre
hook: 3 kg on the left, 1 kg on the right. Move 1 kg across. Does the bag now hang straight?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a bag hangs level when the centre of its load is under the handle, so moving some weight from the heavy side to the light side balances it without removing anything

misconception: As long as the total weight is the same, how you load a bag makes no difference to how it hangs.
objective: The heavier side pulls the balance point towards it, and the bag tilts until that point is under the handle. Move 1 kg across and both sides hold 2 kg, so the bag hangs straight, though it weighs the same.

recall.question: A tote holds 4 kg on the left and 2 kg on the right, each side the same distance from the handle. Without removing anything, what puts the load's centre under the handle?
options: Move 1 kg from left to right
Move 2 kg from left to right
Nothing: 6 kg is 6 kg wherever it sits
recall.why: The centre is a mass-weighted average of positions. With 3 kg on each side at equal distances it sits under the handle, and the total is still 6 kg. Centred is not the same as strong enough.
